stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $PQRS$. Sarika measures $\angle P = \angle Q = \angle R = \angle S = 90^\circ$.

Can she classify $PQRS$ as a rectangle without separately checking that opposite sides are equal?

options.text: Yes: a quadrilateral with all angles $90^\circ$ is a rectangle; opposite-side equalities then follow.
She should call the figure a right angle, not a rectangle.
Yes, even if $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ were only three rays and not a closed quadrilateral.
The same rule also classifies any open broken line of four right turns as a rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: A closed quadrilateral with four right angles is a rectangle; opposite sides then follow. Calling it only a right angle, dropping the closed-quadrilateral condition, or applying the rule to an open path miss that classification.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source grid kite into rectangle PQRS with four right-angle marks.
